featured_reviews.name: Arin Paul
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Bharat, Churchgate, is one of those old-school vegetarian cafés that quietly survives on routine rather than hype. No frills, no experiments, just straightforward food and a steady crowd of office-goers and regulars.

We had Puri Bhaji, Coffee, and Tikki Chole. The puri bhaji was simple and filling, nothing exceptional but nothing to complain about either. The bhaji was mildly spiced, homely in taste, and the puris were fresh enough. The tikki chole was decent; the tikkis were soft and the chole had a familiar North Indian flavour, though it didn’t stand out in any special way. The coffee was basic café-style, served hot, doing its job without trying to impress.

What works in Cafe Bharat’s favour is its budget-friendly pricing, quick service, and convenient location near Churchgate. It’s not a place you’d go out of your way to visit, but if you’re in the area and want a quick, affordable vegetarian meal, it does the job.

The ambience is functional and old-fashioned; clean, but clearly built for efficiency rather than comfort or aesthetics. Service is prompt and no-nonsense.

Overall, Cafe Bharat is reliable, modest, and predictable. Nothing great, nothing bad. Just a simple veg café that knows its role and sticks to it. Suitable for a quick bite, not for culinary excitement.

featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

featured_reviews.name: Manikandan
featured_reviews.review_text: Santosham - Satvik South Indian Restaurant near Marine Drive is a clean and comforting spot for authentic South Indian vegetarian food in South Mumbai. The restaurant keeps a simple, traditional feel without trying to be overly fancy, and the food is the main highlight. Located in Marine Lines, it’s convenient after a walk along Marine Drive or nearby sightseeing. Service is quick, portions are satisfying, and the overall experience feels homely and consistent without being overpriced. featured_reviews.name: RACHNA TULI MASHKARIA
featured_reviews.review_text:
The banana leaf thali is not just a meal – it’s an experience that blends flavor, tradition, and hospitality in the most wholesome way. Served on a fresh banana leaf, the thali immediately brings a sense of authenticity and connection to Indian culinary roots.

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

featured_reviews.name: Sarah Chamdawala
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had an amazing authentic South Indian breakfast at Santosham! Ordered the Mysore sada dosa, which was crispy and spicy and delicious; the ghee podi idli was fluffy and you could really taste the shuddh ghee; the beetroot rawa dosa was soo crispy and had just the perfect little hint of beetroot flavour; the benne dosa was yum and perfectly crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside and served with the most decadent pure white butter! The filter coffees (both cold and hot) were also delicious with the perfect froth on top! We also enjoyed the rose milk with chia seeds. The tomato chutney, coconut chutney and sambhar served on the side were also great and proved the perfect accompaniments to the meal.
A special mention for the service which was top notch, thanks to Nasim and Uday who were very helpful and quick.
10/10 would recommend this place!

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Legacy in Transition: Mani’s Cafe, Mumbai…
Mani’s Cafe remains a cornerstone of Mumbai’s South Indian culinary map, yet recent visits suggest it is currently navigating the fine line between its historic "comfort food" status and the pressures of rapid expansion. Whether you’re at the Matunga original or the newer outposts in Chembur and Dadar, the experience is a mix of high-speed efficiency and slightly inconsistent quality.
The Highlights
The Filter Coffee continues to be the undisputed hero—authentic, "kadak," and consistently excellent across branches. The Pineapple Sheera remains a delightful indulgence, and the Thatte Idli offers that fluffy, cloud-like texture that long-time fans crave. If you stick to these classics, the value-for-money remains unbeatable.
The Challenges
The 3-star rating stems from a noticeable inconsistency in their newer fusion offerings. While "Pizza Idli" and "Matka Dosa" sound innovative, they often lean too heavily on mayonnaise and sauces, masking the traditional flavors. Service at the busier QSR outlets (like Matunga East) can feel rushed, and the lack of seating at many locations means you’re often eating in your car or standing in a crowded lane.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5

If you’re in Fort and craving authentic South Indian food, JM Idli Cafe is an absolute must-visit! It’s one of those rare places that combine delicious food, warm service, and genuine consistency — a true gem in the heart of Mumbai.

I’ve visited JM Idli Cafe multiple times, and every experience has been wonderful. Their menu offers a perfect blend of traditional South Indian favourites and creative variations. But the dish that truly wins my heart every single time is their Mysore Sada Cheese Dosa. It’s absolutely fantastic! The dosa is crisp, golden, and perfectly balanced — the slight spice of the Mysore chutney mixed with the smooth, melted cheese creates a unique and addictive flavour. You can immediately tell it’s made with care and fresh ingredients.

Their idlis are soft and fluffy, the sambar has that comforting homemade taste, and their chutneys are fresh, vibrant, and perfectly seasoned. Even simple dishes like the ghee dosa, upma, and pongal are prepared with attention to detail and taste just right.

The staff here deserve full appreciation as well — they’re polite, attentive, and always serve with a smile. You never have to wait too long, and they make sure every customer feels valued.

The café itself is clean, cosy, and welcoming — perfect for breakfast, lunch, or even a light evening meal. The prices are very reasonable for the quality and portion sizes, which makes it even more worth it.

Overall, JM Idli Cafe is the kind of place that keeps you coming back. Every visit feels satisfying and cheerful. If you love South Indian food or simply enjoy delicious, freshly made meals, you’ll love this spot. And if you visit, don’t miss their Mysore Sada Cheese Dosa — it’s honestly one of the best in Mumbai!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything was just perfect!

Every single dish we ordered was simply amazing. Here is a breakdown of the highlights:
The Iconic Dosas & Idlis: The Ghee Podi Idli was cloud-soft, drenched in flavorful ghee, and packed a perfect spicy punch with the podi. The Benne Butter Masala Dosa was perfectly crisp on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and rich in flavor.
The Chutneys: A special shoutout to their signature chutneys—fresh, vibrant, and the perfect accompaniment to the main dishes.
The Grand Finale: You cannot leave this place without trying their Coffee Ice Cream. It is an absolute game-changer! It perfectly captures the rich, bold, and aromatic essence of traditional filter coffee but in a creamy, refreshing frozen dessert. It’s not overly sweet, making it the ultimate treat for true coffee lovers.
The service was incredibly fast despite the bustling crowd, and the quality of ingredients truly shines through in every bite.

Verdict: Exceptional food, vibrant vibes, and a 10/10 experience. Whether you are going for a heavy breakfast or a sweet evening treat, this place never disappoints. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Rameshwaram Cafe has been on my list for a while, though I walked in with some hesitation given the mixed reviews online. Glad to say, the experience leaned positive.

We ordered the Benne Pudi Masala Dosa, Benne Masala Dosa, Ghee Pudi Idli, and the Filter Coffee Softy. The dosas arrived crisp, generously buttered, and well-balanced in flavour, while the Ghee Pudi Idli stood out for its richness and depth. The Filter Coffee Softy was an interesting, indulgent twist—worth trying for something different.

What works here is consistency in taste and a certain indulgent South Indian profile that’s clearly designed to appeal to a wider palate. However, the pricing does sit on the higher side for this category, which slightly affects the overall value equation.

I visited on a Monday around 3 PM and was seated in about 30 minutes—manageable by their standards. That said, this isn’t a place I’d personally queue up for on a busy weekend. It’s best experienced when the rush is relatively controlled.

If you’re in that part of the city, it’s definitely worth a visit once—more for the experience than as a regular go-to.

I visited the Rameshwaram cafe in Mumbai twice since it opened, and if has been extremely memorable each time.. not just because because of the food, that is soul-soothing as ever!! But what really stood out each time was the hospitality of the staff!! You can see the crowd that gathers outside each day eager to taste the sumptuous food inside and that too in the Mumbai heat and humidity.. that itself is a testament to the quality of food I suppose. But it is the staff who go above and beyond to make the experience as rewarding.. right from the people managing the crowd at the entrance, offering a seat to an aged couple as they wait in line or simply accommodating our request in the sweetest way to allow us seats in a fully booked restaurant just so that our friend (leaving for the UK the very next day) doesn't have to miss out on the experience. featured_reviews.name: Tarun Joseph
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Rameshwaram Cafe at Churchgate this morning for a quick breakfast like old times.
I’m a Kannadiga and I've lived in Bengaluru for a couple of years and used to visit Rameshwaram Cafe (Indiranagar and JP Nagar outlets), at least once a month. Even now, whenever I go back to Bengaluru, it’s a mandatory stop. So when they announced they were opening in Mumbai, I was genuinely excited. I’ve been missing proper dosa and idli here.

But what I ate today was not Rameshwaram Cafe.

I ordered my usual ghee pudi plain dosa and there was barely any pudi on it. The taste was completely off. It didn’t have the flavour, the texture, or even the smell that makes Rameshwaram Cafe what it is. The taste just felt different, very different. It honestly didn’t even feel like the Rameshwaram Cafe I remember from Bengaluru.
I didn’t try the pudi idli myself, but my friends ordered it and said it was just average as well.

After all the hype, the long queues, and the name they’ve built in Bengaluru, this was unbelievably disappointing. If this is what Rameshwaram Cafe Mumbai is serving, they’re just riding on the Bengaluru brand while delivering something far below that standard.

A truly mediocre experience. If you’ve actually eaten at the Bengaluru outlet, this will feel like a huge downgrade.

Oor lives up to its name - absolutely home like food that’s cleverly elevated and ambience with little details of the space reminding of kannadiga elements. I went for my birthday lunch and got delicious rasam rice with a side of banana poriyal. Absolutely delicious walnut halwa (a must have) and refreshing chaas. Every flavor will be familiar, homely and at the same time elevated. Staff is attentive and also mindful in that I felt at ease (and at home/oor). It was lovely to interact with the owner Panchaali and learn about her Mangalore roots and here’s hoping we will see some Mangalore OGs (like bun) on the menu :)

Cannot wait to be back again!

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited OOR Restaurant located at Kitab Mahal, Fort (near Azad Maidan), and it turned out to be a really satisfying South Indian food experience.

Cuisine:
OOR is known for authentic South Indian cuisine, focusing on traditional flavors, classic preparations, and comforting dishes that remind you of home-style food but with restaurant-quality execution.

Ambience:
The ambience is simple, clean, and welcoming. It has a calm and relaxed vibe, making it a great place for a casual meal with family, friends, or even a quick food stop while you’re around the Fort area. The space feels traditional yet comfortable, and perfect if you want to enjoy your food peacefully without too much noise.

What we tried:

☕ Filter Coffee – Strong, aromatic, and perfectly brewed. A must-have to complete the South Indian experience.

🧡 Steamed Idli – Soft, fluffy, and served fresh. Went really well with the chutneys and sambar.

🧅 Irulli Uttapam – Loaded with onions, nicely cooked, and full of flavor. Great texture and taste.

🥘 Paniyaram – Crispy outside, soft inside. A lovely traditional dish that was well made.

🌶️ Playa Uttapam – Unique and flavorful, nicely spiced and well presented.

🍛 OOR Thali – A complete meal with a variety of South Indian items. Perfect if you want to try multiple flavors at once. Very filling and satisfying.

Service & Management:
Service was smooth, staff was polite, and the overall management was well-handled. Food came on time and everything was served properly.

Overall:
If you’re someone who loves authentic South Indian food, OOR is definitely a spot to add to your bucket list — especially when you’re in the Fort area. Great food, good service, and a comforting dining experience. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

featured_reviews.name: Saurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered veg biryani from Taste of Kerala on 13 October 2025, but I was delivered chicken biryani instead. This is a serious issue, especially for someone who does not eat non-veg.
I immediately went to the restaurant and showed them the delivered order. They said the owner was not present and asked me to return the food and come back the next day for a refund. I trusted them and handed over the food.
When I returned the next day, the owner refused to take responsibility and told me to contact Zomato instead. This was extremely unprofessional and dishonest.
This is not just a mistake—it’s a serious concern when non-veg food is served while claiming it is veg. Please be very careful. If the intention was to avoid a refund, they could have been honest instead of wasting my time.
I do not recommend this restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Rituka Nakhawa
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Taste of Kerala and had a really good experience overall. The place serves tasty, authentic food with nice service. Due to the crowd, the staff does struggle a bit with serving everyone on time, but they still manage with a positive attitude.
We tried the Sunday Special Veg Banana Meal, Coconut Chilly Roasted Chicken with Kerala Paratha, and Chicken Kizhi Parotha. Every dish was absolutely delicious — rich flavours and true Kerala taste. We’ll definitely be visiting again!
A special mention to the manager, who was extremely warm and attentive. He personally checked on every table, and when he noticed we enjoyed the payasam, he even served us some extra. Such gestures really make the experience memorable. 💛🌴✨

featured_reviews.name: sankeertha varanasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai Masala is a new cozy Vegetarian restaurant in Narayanguda.
When you enter the place you witness fancy lightning column, sleek orange interiors which creates the fun, joy and playfulness atmosphere. Orange is a great colour choice because it stimulates the appetite and also encourages social interaction. Being foodaholic, I like everything from street food, fast food joints to cafe's and regular restaurants. This place is serving varity of cuisines with finest quality taste which makes this place interesting. If you wanna have thalis, proper north Indian and south indian food or any quick bites head here if you find yourself around. Each section on the menu has the timings written for when the dishes are available. Starting off with mocktails tried blue lagoon and Virgin mojito which were okay. Also, tried sweet Lassi and Oreo Milkshake according to me milkshake needs little improvisation.
Moving on to the appetizers section tried Crunchy manchurian dry which was spicy, crisp faultlessly tossed tasted great. Crispy Corn makes a ideal starter for veg's and it was palatable.
Chinese Bhel: This is my all time favourite chat which is made with fried noodles perked up with crunchy vegetables which was so appetizing.
Italian Paniyaram: This balls were made with green's and others veggies coated with breadcrumbs and deep fried topped with cheese.
Rumali Masala Papad topped with Indian chopped masala, lime, coriander and finely chopped fresh veggies. Nachos were served with cheese and bean's were flawless.
Vol-au-vents: It's a puff pastry stuffed with corn delivered maximum flavour when paired with cheese.
Vada Pav Dabeli Combo name itself says it's a combination snack the pav has both dabeli and vada pav flavour
Mumbai Masala Pizza: The pizza was quite good with a desi twist and loaded with lots of veggies, paneer and cheese.
Masala Garlic bread: Desi garlic bread tasted good and was having the perfect amount of the cheese and veggies added to it.
Pav Bhaji: It was served piping hot with flavourful bhaji
Moving to the much anticipated main course Mumbai Masala didn't disappoint one little bit. Veg Chatpat and Paneer Toofani were the curries of the day which were very well enjoyed with the hot, fluffy and soft breads. Paneer Toofani was having to kinds of curries half of the curry tasted like butter paneer masala and the other half tasted like palak paneer which was served in cabbage leaf. Coming to breads tried Lachha paratha, Kashmiri paratha, Lal mirch ka Paratha, kothmir butter naan, Chilli garlic naan, Masala kulcha, Kothmir butter roti and butter naan. Tried combination fried rice which was served with wet manchurian with an awesome presentation. Lastly, from the main course tried veg dum biryani which was soulful.
As, for desserts they don't have elaborate menu. Tried moong dal ka halwa set to perfection with drizzle of dry fruits. Sundae icecream was also good.
The service staff was pleasingly hospitable making sure there was never ever a moment where the diner's are waiting with empty plates.
Overall Taste:4/5
Service:5/5
Presentation:5/5

featured_reviews.name: Indrayudh Roy
featured_reviews.review_text: Relaxing ambience, there's two seating sections and some weird glasswork that appeals to me. It's next to a cake shop which doesn't seem to be doing much in the way of God. I recommend trying there American Chop Suey and I think for South Indian food lovers, there dosas are quite fine. Unnecessarily long menu when it comes to Indian vegetable dishes; they would do better to include better starters and perhaps innovate on their Chinese offerings. For those who are getting hot thinking of the Chinese New Year, you might celebrate it here. Honestly, I was relieved that they have a good menu rather than just serving idlis and dosas. Atmosphere is cool -- the talk devolved into the discussion of basic macro-economics, demand, supply and the falsity of inflation due to the loopholes in the Credit System.

Since there is no much affordable pure veg hotels around had to go here. If there is any other you find you can skip this place.

featured_reviews.name: Rahul Kurup
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited this spot in Fort and was blown away by the authentic flavors. The Kerala Parotta was perfectly flaky, and pairing it with the tender mutton fry was the highlight of my meal. I also highly recommend the banana leaf thali for a true traditional experience—the variety of sides is impressive. The staff is very attentive, especially with recommendations, and the service is surprisingly quick despite the lunch rush. It's a great value-for-money find for anyone craving genuine South Indian cuisine in the city. Don't forget to end your meal with their delicious Payasam!

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Many diners enjoy the authentic Kerala-style dishes — both vegetarian and non-vegetarian. For instance, the vegetarian thali served on a banana leaf gets repeated mentions for its “homely” flavour and variety.  ￼
•	The restaurant is considered value-for-money, especially given its central Fort location. One guide mentions:
“A really hearty non vegetarian meal for two could cost up to INR 1,000 but could be as low as INR 500 as well.”  ￼
•	Friendly and welcoming staff is cited often:
“The people who served us were very kind and helpful.”  ￼
•	Strong recommendation for seafood lovers: prawns, fish curry/fry items are frequently recommended.  ￼
•	Good for a casual meal with a local flavour — not high-end luxury, but genuine in feel.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Date - 07 Jun 26
Time - 2155
Table no. - 17
I had a very disappointing experience at this hotel. The food quality was below expectations, lacking both taste and freshness. The dishes were not prepared well, and the overall dining experience was unsatisfactory.
In addition, the staff behavior was not professional or welcoming. The service was slow, and the staff seemed uninterested in addressing customer concerns. Good hospitality is an important part of any dining experience, but unfortunately, it was missing here.
Overall, I would not recommend this hotel based on my experience. There is significant room for improvement in both food quality and customer service.

featured_reviews.name: Betina John
featured_reviews.review_text: A quiet spot that serves authentic keralite dishes. You get a glass of chukkuvellam, along with your food, which is a pink colored water which doesn't taste any different than ordinary warm water but it's a traditional ayurvedic drink known for It's medicinal properties. The dishes are incredibly spicy but delicious. Since we were a little late, the payasam (dessert) got over. Hopefully next time we're there, will grab some. Loved the experience and warmth.
